evidence: Caes. BG 4.12.4: amplissimō genere nātus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.180: quī nōbilī genere nātī sunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Birth and family; the word’s other common senses are a race or people and, above all, a kind or sort (Lewis & Short). For upbringing and schooling see education.

evidence: Cic. Planc. 60: summō locō nātus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fl. 24: īnfimō locō nātus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of rank and standing, with an adjective: summō, īnfimō locō nātus.

phrases.latin: C. Laelius, cum eī quīdam malō genere nātus dīceret, indignum esse suīs majōribus, at hercule, inquit, tū tuīs dignus
phrases.english: When a man of low birth told Gaius Laelius that he was unworthy of his ancestors, “But you, by Hercules,” he said, “are worthy of yours.”
Tanaquil, a woman of the highest birth

sources: Lewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: locus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
